paul-tonge.name: Paul Tonge
paul-tonge.bio: Paul Tonge is an English composer, sound designer, sound-driver developer and music director whose game-audio career began in the late 1980s. He co-founded the Sound Images audio company with Tony Williams, later worked with Software Creations, and accumulated credits across C64, Amiga, console and handheld games.

peter-clarke.name: Peter Clarke
peter-clarke.bio: Peter Clarke was a British composer whose C64 work became associated with Ocean Software and related projects. His credits include Bubble Bobble, Head over Heels and other home-computer titles, drawing on a background in keyboards, guitar and electronic music production.

peter-mcconnell.name: Peter McConnell
peter-mcconnell.bio: Peter McConnell is an American composer and musician whose career includes LucasArts, independent game scoring and major modern productions. He helped develop the iMUSE system and contributed music to Monkey Island, Indiana Jones, Grim Fandango and later titles including Psychonauts 2 and Broken Age.

ramiro-vaca.name: Ramiro Vaca
ramiro-vaca.bio: Ramiro Vaca is a German composer and scene musician whose game work includes music for Rainbow Arts and Kaiko. His C64 credits in the CCG archive include R-Type and Turrican, and interviews document a background in both music and the German C64 scene.

randy-glover.name: Randy Glover
randy-glover.bio: Randy Glover is an American designer, programmer, artist and musician best known for creating Jumpman and for work at Epyx. His CCG music credits include Jumpman and Summer Games, reflecting the multi-discipline way many early game creators handled both code and audio.

reyn-ouwehand.name: Reyn Ouwehand
reyn-ouwehand.bio: Reyn Ouwehand is a Dutch composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist whose professional music career began with computer-game commissions while he was still a teenager. His C64 work includes Last Ninja 3 and Flimbo’s Quest, after which he built a wider career as a producer, arranger and studio musician.

richard-joseph.name: Richard Joseph
richard-joseph.bio: Richard Joseph was a British composer, sound designer and audio director whose career covered the C64, Amiga and later game platforms. He worked on titles including Barbarian, Cannon Fodder, The Chaos Engine and Sensible Soccer, and became known for pushing interactive music, speech and licensed-artist collaboration in games.

rob-hartshorne.name: Rob Hartshorne
rob-hartshorne.bio: Rob Hartshorne is a British media composer whose early computer-game work included a partnership with Graham Jarvis through Clever Music. His C64 credits include Back to the Future, Blade Runner, The Rocky Horror Show and Shao-Lin's Road, while later work extended heavily into television music.

rob-hubbard.name: Rob Hubbard
rob-hubbard.bio: Rob Hubbard is an English composer and programmer whose Commodore 64 music became one of the defining sounds of 1980s game audio. His C64 catalogue includes Commando, Monty on the Run, International Karate, Master of Magic and many other titles, and he later worked in the United States for Electronic Arts. Reliable biographical sources give his birth year as 1956; a precise public birth date has not been established.

robert-westgate.name: Robert Westgate
robert-westgate.bio: Robert Westgate is a British C64-era musician whose documented credits include Guzzler and By Fair Means or Foul, along with other 8-bit game-audio work. Public biographical information is limited, so the profile is based on preserved game-credit records.

rudolf-stember.name: Rudolf Stember
rudolf-stember.bio: Rudolf Stember is a German composer and audio director whose career began with home-computer music before moving into major game-development roles. He worked with Rainbow Arts and later Factor 5, with CCG-linked credits including Curse of Ra and The Secret of Monkey Island.

russell-lieblich.name: Russell Lieblich
russell-lieblich.bio: Russell Lieblich was an American composer, musician and sound designer who moved from academic music and physics into the early games industry. He worked at Mattel and Activision and wrote music for titles including Master of the Lamps, Little Computer People and Ghostbusters; later work extended into Electronic Arts and other game-audio projects.
